layerLabel: Real geological sites — comparisons, not identified Book of Mormon cities
interpretation: The Book of Mormon is treated as a historical account for reconstruction. None of these observed events is established as its destruction event. Date labels describe the cited evidence; they are not all equivalent probability intervals.

markers.name: Popocatépetl · Lorenzo pumice
markers.coordinateMeaning: Smithsonian volcano location; not a Tetimpa excavation coordinate or proposed city
markers.datePrecision: Approximate estimate; full sample probability intervals not verified
markers.summary: Real explosive eruption and affected settlements. Older Tetimpa research placed burial in AD 50–100; newer Lorenzo pumice research dates the event to about 40 BCE. Do not present it as a verified AD 34 eruption or identify a named city.

markers.name: Ilopango · Tierra Blanca Joven
markers.coordinateMeaning: Smithsonian caldera location; not a proposed city
markers.datePrecision: Published uncertainty; different from a generic approximate range
markers.textEvent: Possible volcanic darkness and burial mechanism: 3 Nephi 8:19–23
markers.summary: Powerful eruption provides a physical analogue, but its published fifth-century date is centuries too late for the AD 33–34 target. The older 539/540 proposal also fails that target. No Book of Mormon city identified.

markers.name: Barú · early catalogued eruption
markers.coordinateMeaning: Smithsonian volcano location; not a proposed city
markers.datePrecision: Catalog uncertainty, not a verified AD 34 occurrence
markers.summary: Panama has real volcanic mechanisms. This listed eruption range does not reach AD 34. An incomplete catalog leaves research open but does not establish a missing eruption or settlement match.

markers.name: New Madrid seismic zone · 1811–1812
markers.coordinateMeaning: USGS catalog estimate for the 16 December 1811 08:15 UTC earthquake; historical epicenter uncertain and estimates differ
markers.datePrecision: Historical event dates; coordinate is an estimated epicenter
markers.textEvent: Ground failure and water replacing land: 3 Nephi 8:13–18; 9:6–8
markers.summary: Inland earthquakes can cause liquefaction, alter drainage, and create lakes; volcanic arcs are not the only regions with ground-failure mechanisms. This sequence is far too late. Paleoseismic events around AD 300, 900, and 1450 do not establish an AD 34 match.
